Confirmed via retry (image_id 242): NOT a kernel panic - this is a distinct failure mode, a semaphore livelock in libnvram.so's own NVRAM shim init (sem_get()/nvram.c:58-113). The wait loop is a tight busy-spin with NO sleep between iterations (1000x semctl() checking sem_otime), which rules out host-speed/timing sensitivity as the cause - it either resolves in microseconds or fails 100% deterministically. Evidence: repeated "sem_get: Waiting for semaphore timeout" + "sem_lock: Unable to get semaphore!" for the entire check-mode window, never breaking out, until the 900s check-mode ceiling kills it. Working theory: the process that wins the semget(IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL) race fails its own semop() init call (nvram.c:86) and deletes the semaphore, leaving every other reader spinning against an ID that will never get sem_otime set. Root cause not yet fully traced (would need guest-side IPC limits/dmesg inspection); distinct from and unrelated to the time_zone panic bug.
